plan.title: Verstappen Wins Las Vegas GP by 0.639 Seconds
plan.description: Max Verstappen won the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix after a race-long fight with the Mercedes pair, holding off Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds. Here is how the final laps turned the podium upside down, and what comes next.

beats.narration: Less than one second. That is all that separated the winner from second place after fifty laps under the lights of Las Vegas. Max Verstappen took the win by just 0.639 seconds.

props.label: Verstappen's winning margin over Lando Norris

beats.narration: The race was run on November 21st, 2026, on the streets of Nevada. It was a thrilling and frenetic Grand Prix, and for Verstappen, the four-time World Champion, it was his third win in Las Vegas.

First, the Las Vegas night race itself, a street circuit glowing under the lights. Then, Max Verstappen and his Red Bull car, which led a race-long fight against the Mercedes pair of Russell and Antonelli.

props.alt: Las Vegas night race and Verstappen's Red Bull

beats.narration: Here is how it unfolded. First came the battle for the lead between Verstappen and George Russell. Then Russell had a lock-up with three laps left. That sent him off the track, and he fell back to ninth.
The late drama reshaped the podium. Russell had a lock-up and finished ninth. Antonelli then had an issue at Turn 16 and finished fourth. That left the McLaren pair to take the podium.
The final podium was Max Verstappen for Red Bull with 25 points, Lando Norris second for McLaren with 18, and Oscar Piastri third, 1.529 seconds behind the winner, with 15.
Behind them, Kimi Antonelli was fourth for Mercedes. Pierre Gasly took an impressive fifth for Alpine, and his teammate Franco Colapinto was sixth. Carlos Sainz was eighth for Williams.
Ferrari had an eventful night. Lewis Hamilton recovered from eleventh on the grid to finish seventh, despite a ten-second penalty and contact with teammate Charles Leclerc, who finished tenth.
Not everyone finished. Arvid Lindblad spun behind the Safety Car and retired, Sergio Perez and Alex Albon also did not finish, and Fernando Alonso retired one lap before the end.

What comes next? The Qatar Grand Prix, the penultimate round of the 2026 season, on November 27th to 29th at Lusail. After Vegas, the takeaway is simple: in this season, never count anyone out until the flag.
